content.text:
You were right to insist on a real status effect. The current engine behavior is:

- Carry capacity: `max stamina × 0.60 kg`, including passive stamina bonuses.
- Above 85% capacity: player is `encumbered`/burdened and stamina regeneration is reduced to 50%.
- Above 100%: stamina regeneration becomes 0% and diagonal movement is forced into cardinal movement.
- Above 125%: pickup and auto-pickup are refused.

Where it belongs:

- Thresholds and tuning: [`encumbranceTuning.js`](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/data/encumbranceTuning.js)
- Pure calculation and pickup predicate: [`encumbrance.js`](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/utils/encumbrance.js)
- Canonical conditional status creation/removal: [`encumbranceSystem.js`](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/systems/encumbranceSystem.js)
- Status definition/description: [`effectDefs.js`](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/data/effectDefs.js)
- Stamina consequence: [`staminaRegenerationSystem.js`](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/systems/staminaRegenerationSystem.js)
- Movement consequence: [`movementSystem.js`](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/systems/movementSystem.js)
- Pickup limit: [`itemPickupSystem.js`](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/systems/itemPickupSystem.js)

One important distinction: `encumbered` should represent the 85%+ condition. It should not replace the separate overloaded tier, because overload has additional effects. We should either retain `Encumbrance.overloaded` as the derived tier or eventually add a separate conditional `overloaded` status.
